agents.name: claude
agents.description: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed.

agents.name: Explore
agents.description: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.

agents.name: moontaehyung:auditor
agents.description: Independently audits RIS research coverage, evidence integrity, plan feasibility, assumptions, and forecasts.

agents.name: moontaehyung:designer
agents.description: Produces interactive RIS research HTML from canonical Markdown through Archify.

agents.name: moontaehyung:engineer
agents.description: Assesses RIS candidate feasibility and defines technical configurations, verification methods and acceptance criteria, and runs authorized verification.

agents.name: moontaehyung:planner
agents.description: Turns RIS goals and evidence into a branching project plan, conditional forecasts, risks, gates, and fallback routes.

agents.name: moontaehyung:researcher
agents.description: Investigates technical questions, approach families, evidence, contrary findings, and research coverage for RIS projects.

agents.name: Plan
agents.description: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.

agents.name: statusline-setup
agents.description: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting.

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: moontaehyung:aar
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Conduct an After Action Review of completed or interrupted work, comparing expectations with outcomes and capturing successful practices, lessons, and follow-up actions. Use for broad task or team retrospectives; use RCA for deeper investigation of a specific failure.

commands.name: moontaehyung:analysis-router
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Select and coordinate AAR, RCA, RMEA, FTA, MCDA, risk planning, ADR, and verification workflows when a request crosses their boundaries or needs multiple analyses. Resolve consequential ambiguity by comparing candidate workflows independently through auto-subagents; skip routing overhead for an obvious local task.

commands.name: moontaehyung:archify
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Create validated architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, lifecycle/state, ERD, class, tree, timeline, and waterfall diagrams as explorable standalone HTML with dark/light themes, motion and image/SVG/WebM export. Accept requirements or Mermaid; inspect repository evidence for code-backed diagrams. Use when visualizing systems, API calls, pipelines, schemas, histories, timings, or everyday steps, parts, relationships and states. Also turn an answer into a one-page explainer, with the conclusion first, structured panels, native diagrams and charts, when the user asks for a page, an explainer or an answer to share (做成一页, 用页面讲), or proactively when the user's rules opt in with an [archify explainer: ...] line. Not for dashboards.

commands.name: moontaehyung:architecture-decision-record
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Create, amend, supersede, and audit Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) documenting architectural choices, alternative options, evidence, trade-offs, risk ownership, consequences, and reversal triggers. Use when a technical decision is proposed, accepted, revisited, or reversed; pair with project-plan for branching project plans.

commands.name: moontaehyung:auto-skill-manager
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Use when the user asks which skills fit a project or task, requests skill/plugin-package inventory or observation review, or asks for scoped Skill Manager CLI maintenance. Use skill-creator to author skill content and plugin-management for external app integrations.

commands.name: moontaehyung:auto-subagents
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Assess and coordinate useful parallel work and subagent delegation across tasks, including investigation, implementation, and verification, when independence and expected benefit justify the overhead.

commands.name: moontaehyung:create-gui
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Design and build new stateful desktop operator GUI projects through a persistent, multi-session requirements interview, documented approval gate, implementation, and interaction/error-path verification. Applies to hardware-backed, simulation, replay, and data-driven operator applications; do not route ordinary small edits to an established GUI here.

commands.name: moontaehyung:design-boundaries
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Design responsibility, dependency, state, and lifecycle boundaries for new systems, substantial features, or scoped architectural redesigns. Use when multiple capabilities or resource owners must collaborate; do not trigger for routine local fixes or split modules solely by line count.

commands.name: moontaehyung:explain-xlsx
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Create formula-traceable XLSX workbooks alongside code-derived numerical results. Use across simulation, research, engineering, analytics, operations, and other quantitative projects when producing a reportable result artifact, or when asked to explain calculations in a workbook. Not for routine data export or unrelated spreadsheet editing.

commands.name: moontaehyung:faust
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Estimate the probability of a defined event using information available at a cutoff. Use for prospective forecasts, historical case exercises from supplied evidence, and scoring resolved predictions. Also supports stock research and RIS project handoffs.

commands.name: moontaehyung:fta
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Perform Fault Tree Analysis of a defined undesirable event using AND/OR logic, event definitions, minimal cut sets, and mitigations. Use for prospective failure-path analysis or incident hypotheses; an FTA alone does not establish the actual cause of an incident.

commands.name: moontaehyung:maintain-boundaries
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Keep responsibility, dependency, state, and lifecycle boundaries intact while extending or refactoring existing code. Use for cross-module changes, shared resource or contract changes, and edits to highly coupled controllers; do not require architecture reviews for trivial local edits.

commands.name: moontaehyung:mcda
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Compare alternatives using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis with explicit criteria, scales, weights, evidence, and sensitivity analysis. Use for consequential trade-offs across multiple criteria; record architectural decisions in an available ADR workflow when appropriate.

commands.name: moontaehyung:modify-gui
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Modify an existing stateful desktop operator GUI and the backend behavior directly required by that GUI through persistent change interviews, impact analysis, explicit approval, implementation, and end-to-end regression verification. Applies to hardware-backed, simulation, replay, and data-driven operator applications; do not route tiny isolated presentation fixes or backend work unrelated to a user-visible GUI contract here.

commands.name: moontaehyung:project-plan
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Design or revise consequential project plans with branching choices, quality gates, fallback routes, and evidence-based switch criteria. Coordinate specialist risk or option analysis only when needed; standalone risk registers belong to RMEA, weighted alternative evaluation to MCDA, and material architectural decision history to ADR.

commands.name: moontaehyung:rca
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Investigate actual important failures, recurring defects, and unexplained outcome gaps using causal hypotheses, supporting and contrary evidence, and corrective-action checks. Use AAR for overall retrospectives and FTA for modeled failure combinations; obvious local errors need no formal RCA.

commands.name: moontaehyung:research-audit
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Independently audit RIS research coverage, evidence quality, causal integrity, plan feasibility, and conditional forecasts before project pre-analysis is accepted.

commands.name: moontaehyung:reviewer
commands.description: (moontaehyung) 연구 논문, 기술 보고서, 발표자료를 엄격하고 근거 중심으로 심사해 거절·감점 위험, 근거 부족, 우선순위별 보완안을 제시할 때 사용합니다.

commands.name: moontaehyung:ris
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Initialize or resume project-local research, align the agent with the user's background, investigate phenomena, causes and solution families, organize source-backed learning and branching plans, and record findings or handoffs in Markdown for Obsidian. Use for RIS requests and research continuity in initialized projects. Also use for explicit requests to diagnose or improve the RIS skill or its role instructions. Do not initialize unrelated projects or record every conversation automatically.

commands.name: moontaehyung:rmea
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Perform Risk Mode and Effect Analysis to identify potential risk modes, their causes and impacts, existing controls, response priorities, and residual risk. Use for structured prospective risk assessment; use FTA for logical combinations producing a specific failure.

commands.name: moontaehyung:skill-auto-manager
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Find and compare reusable products, components, projects, tools, skills and plugins when planning a system or substantial feature, investigating existing alternatives, authoring skills, or addressing capability gaps and repeated manual work. Apply even when the user does not mention skills or plugins. Also review installed skill coverage and inventory. Skip routine work already covered; use skill-creator for authoring and plugin-management for app connections.

commands.name: moontaehyung:teach-me
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Explain a real computation, algorithm, formula, or code path so a non-specialist can reproduce a worked example by hand. Use when the user explicitly asks to learn how a calculation works step by step, not for a short definition or routine code summary.

commands.name: moontaehyung:update-architecture
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Refresh a project's current architecture documents and non-expert HTML reader only when explicitly requested, preserving separate change explanations and verified evidence.

commands.name: moontaehyung:verify-check
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Split substantial code or behavior changes into small, independently verifiable steps, verify their handoffs, and validate the original user workflow. Use for multi-step or cross-layer implementation, fixes, and reviews; scale checks to risk. Use rca when failures need deeper cause analysis.

commands.name: moontaehyung:Zotero
commands.description: (moontaehyung) Use Zotero Desktop from Codex to search a local library, verify reference metadata and recommendation evidence, read indexed full text when requested, export BibTeX, insert citation keys, and import verified records. Never invent references or fill bibliographic gaps from memory.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Sync a React design system to Claude Design. Bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design."

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read FIRST, before you answer, run a command or open a file (already started? read it now); don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file; if nothing hits, load this skill).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a theme, a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
